title: How wide is each signal
idea: CW is a few hundred hertz, SSB about 3 kHz, AM twice that, FM wider still. Leave room for the station next door, match your receiver's filter to the signal, and don't overmodulate.

rows: Excessive bandwidth; vertical lines on a waterfall

compare.how: About 150 Hz wide; leave 150 to 500 Hz.
About 2.8 kHz wide; leave 2 to 3 kHz.

traps.why: That's SSB spacing. CW needs only 150 to 500 Hz.
Overmodulation makes the signal too wide, not too narrow.

traps.wrong: It is required by FCC rules
traps.why: It's not a rule; it gives the best signal-to-noise ratio.

traps.wrong: Lower symbol rates require wider bandwidth
traps.why: The other way round: faster symbols, wider signal.
Vertical lines either side of a data signal mean overmodulation.
